intent: fix trio from the cl-strategy field case: reference-notes reclassified as mixed dir, --dry-run gates --migrate-layout, dashboard surfaces update failures
notes: **Field case (cl-strategy)**: a user reference note committed at `.gator/reference-notes/` — the DOCUMENTED user location — made the resolver classify the repo `mixed`, `gator update` refused, and the Dashboard swallowed the refusal. Three fixes, Architect-directed:

**Fix 1 — resolver reclassification** (`gator_layout.py`, both copies): `reference-notes` moved from `SHIPPED_DIRECTORIES` (wholesale) to `MIXED_DIRECTORY_SHIPPED_DEFAULTS` (per-filename, template-derived preferred; 16-name bootstrap fallback). User notes at root = valid v2; shipped-named files at root = still mixed. `migrate_layout` Step 6 gains reference-notes (preserve user files at root); Step 5 no longer sweeps the dir wholesale. `test_shipped_dir_duplicates_get_removed` rewritten for the new semantics (shipped-name dup convergence + user-note preservation); new `TestReferenceNotesReclassification` (3 pins incl. the field case).

**Fix 2 — `--dry-run` gates `--migrate-layout`** (`gator-update.py`, both copies): previously the combination EXECUTED the migration (real moves + hook regeneration under a no-changes flag — it migrated a user repo during diagnosis). Gate fires in `main()` before template resolution, prints current layout + real-run instruction. Pin: `TestMigrateDryRunGate` (capfd — `ensure_utf8_stdout` re-wraps stdout).

**Fix 3 — dashboard surfaces failures** (issue #1; `fleet.js` update + gatorize handlers): backend always returned the CLI output; the frontend hid it in a hover tooltip on a red `!`. Both handlers now also `alert()` the output on error and on fetch exception.
Live-verified on cl-strategy: resolves v2 with the note at root, dry-run truly dry, update ran clean (pin 2.9.1, residue committed there as `459f96a`). Suites: base+contracts 908 pass (+4).
Charters: layout (reclassification + WHY), repo-lifecycle (Step-6 sync obligation + dry-run gate), dashboard (surface-don't-mark tripwire).
